# Bundled Semgrep rules

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_rules_doc.py; do not edit by hand. -->

reposcan ships 25 original, MIT-licensed Semgrep rules in `src/reposcan/data/semgrep-rules.yml`.
They run offline (no registry access, no telemetry) and are deliberately **high-precision**: each pattern
targets a construct that is rarely legitimate, and each rule has both a vulnerable and a safe test case.
This is a baseline, not a complete SAST ruleset. Bring your own rules for real coverage:

```toml
[scanners.semgrep]
rules = ["rules/team-rules.yml"]   # relative to the reposcan config file
```

Severity mapping: Semgrep `ERROR` becomes **high**, `WARNING` becomes **medium** (see the
[user guide](user-guide.md#the-unified-finding)).

| Rule id | Languages | Severity | CWE | What it flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reposcan.python.sql-string-concat` | Python | high | CWE-89 | SQL query built by string concatenation; use parameterised queries. |
| `reposcan.python.subprocess-shell-true` | Python | high | CWE-78 | subprocess call with shell=True; pass an argument list instead. |
| `reposcan.python.eval-call` | Python | high | CWE-95 | eval() on dynamic input can execute arbitrary code. |
| `reposcan.python.weak-hash` | Python | medium | CWE-327 | MD5/SHA-1 are broken for security purposes; use SHA-256 or better. |
| `reposcan.python.yaml-unsafe-load` | Python | high | CWE-502 | yaml.load without a safe Loader can construct arbitrary objects; use yaml.safe_load. |
| `reposcan.python.pickle-load` | Python | high | CWE-502 | pickle can execute arbitrary code while loading; never unpickle untrusted data. |
| `reposcan.python.exec-call` | Python | high | CWE-95 | exec() on dynamic input can execute arbitrary code. |
| `reposcan.python.os-system` | Python | high | CWE-78 | os.system() runs a shell command; pass an argument list to subprocess.run instead. |
| `reposcan.python.requests-verify-false` | Python | high | CWE-295 | TLS certificate verification is disabled (verify=False). |
| `reposcan.python.ssl-unverified-context` | Python | high | CWE-295 | An SSL context without certificate verification accepts any server certificate. |
| `reposcan.python.tempfile-mktemp` | Python | medium | CWE-377 | tempfile.mktemp() is race-prone; use tempfile.mkstemp() or NamedTemporaryFile(). |
| `reposcan.python.flask-debug-enabled` | Python | medium | CWE-489 | Running with debug=True exposes an interactive debugger; never enable it in production. |
| `reposcan.js.eval-call` | JavaScript, TypeScript | high | CWE-95 | eval() on dynamic input can execute arbitrary code. |
| `reposcan.js.new-function` | JavaScript, TypeScript | high | CWE-95 | new Function() compiles a string to code at runtime and is equivalent to eval(). |
| `reposcan.js.child-process-command-injection` | JavaScript, TypeScript | high | CWE-78 | A shell command is built from dynamic strings; use execFile/spawn with an argument array. |
| `reposcan.js.html-injection-sink` | JavaScript, TypeScript | medium | CWE-79 | Assigning dynamic strings to innerHTML/outerHTML or document.write enables cross-site scripting. |
| `reposcan.js.tls-verification-disabled` | JavaScript, TypeScript | high | CWE-295 | TLS certificate verification is disabled. |
| `reposcan.js.weak-hash` | JavaScript, TypeScript | medium | CWE-327 | MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for security purposes; use SHA-256 or better. |
| `reposcan.go.insecure-skip-verify` | Go | high | CWE-295 | InsecureSkipVerify disables TLS certificate verification. |
| `reposcan.go.exec-shell-command` | Go | high | CWE-78 | A shell is invoked with a dynamic command string; call the program directly with separate arguments. |
| `reposcan.go.weak-hash` | Go | medium | CWE-327 | MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for security purposes; use SHA-256 or better. |
| `reposcan.go.sql-string-building` | Go | high | CWE-89 | SQL is built by string concatenation or Sprintf; use placeholders and arguments. |
| `reposcan.java.weak-digest` | Java | medium | CWE-327 | MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for security purposes; use SHA-256 or better. |
| `reposcan.java.runtime-exec` | Java | high | CWE-78 | Runtime.exec() with a dynamic command string enables command injection; use ProcessBuilder with an argument list. |
| `reposcan.java.sql-concatenation` | Java | high | CWE-89 | SQL is built by string concatenation; use PreparedStatement with parameters. |

## Testing the rules

Every rule is covered by annotated files in `tests/semgrep/` (`# ruleid: <id>` on the line before code
that must match, `# ok: <id>` before look-alike code that must not). Run the real harness:

```bash
pytest -m integration -k bundled_semgrep     # uses Semgrep's own `semgrep --test`
```

A plain unit test (no Semgrep needed) also checks that every rule has metadata and at least one positive and
one negative test case. When you add a rule, add both cases and regenerate this page with
`python scripts/generate_rules_doc.py`.
